deliverables: Upgrade Cardano mainnet protocol from version 10.0 to 11.0 while remaining in the Conway era.
Enable new Plutus primitives defined in CIP-0109, CIP-0132, CIP-0133, CIP-0138 and CIP-0153.
Make all Plutus built-in functions consistently available across Plutus V1, V2 and V3.
Add UPLC case expressions for Bool, Integer and Data.
Promote or tighten several ledger and node validation, diagnostics, and security rules.
request.recipient: not applicable; no treasury recipient is stated in document
request.what: Initiate an intra-era Cardano mainnet hard fork to Protocol Version 11.0, called the van Rossem hard fork.

claims.claim: The proposal would upgrade Cardano mainnet to protocol version 11.0 through an intra-era hard fork while remaining in the Conway era.
The hard fork would introduce new Plutus primitives for modular exponentiation, dropList, BLS12-381 multi-scalar multiplication, Array, and MaryEraValue as defined in five referenced CIPs.
The proposer claims the Plutus changes will increase script performance, reduce execution cost, and extend what builders can accomplish in Plutus.
The proposal states all Plutus built-ins will become available across Plutus V1, V2, and V3, expanding capabilities for existing V1 and V2 scripts.
The proposal claims ledger consistency and security will improve by enforcing VRF key hash uniqueness at the ledger level and promoting certain checks to ledger predicates.

The proposer states testing reports demonstrate no behavioral regressions, complete conformance between specification and implementation for new ledger rules, and correct operation of new Plutus primitives and case expressions.
The referenced Cardano Node 11.0.1 performance report is cited as showing no regressions for standard value, Plutus, and voting benchmarks and acceptable baseline performance for new Plutus features.

The proposal states at least 85% of stake pools by active stake should have upgraded to a node version capable of protocol version 11 before ratification, with readiness verified by the Constitutional Committee and SPOs supported by Intersect's Hard Fork Working Group.
The proposal states no new protocol parameters are introduced or deprecated, and cost model entries for the new primitives are handled by a separate protocol parameter update governance action.

The reversion plan says the hard fork is a permanent ledger-rule change, with reversion only possible through the CIP-0135 disaster recovery process and possible disabling of Plutus primitives through cost model settings if issues are discovered.

summary: The document proposes a no-treasury hard fork to Cardano protocol version 11.0, presenting Plutus capability and performance improvements, ledger-rule tightening, node diagnostics, guardrail consistency, readiness conditions, and a limited reversion path.
